problems.title: A line-parabola intersection
problems.question: A lies in the first quadrant on y=x² and y=3x+b, and its y-coordinate is twice its x-coordinate. Find b.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: x²=2x gives x=0 or 2. First-quadrant membership selects x=2, y=4.

problems.title: Rationalize then denest
problems.question: Evaluate[1/√18+1/(6−3√2)−1/(√2+1)]·√(27+18√2)/√8.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
steps: The bracket is(4−2√2)/3. Multiplying by(3+3√2)/(2√2) gives 1.

problems.title: Insufficient tangent data
problems.question: Two disjoint circles have radius ratio1:3. The quadratic mean of their common external and internal tangent lengths is 12. Find the harmonic mean of the radii.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: Let radii r,3r and centre distance d>4r. Tangent lengths squared are d²−4r² and d²−16r². Their squared quadratic mean is d²−10r²=144.
steps: This only gives d²=144+10r²; it does not fix r. The harmonic mean is 2r·3r/(r+3r)=3r/2.
For r=1, d=√154, the mean is 1.5. For r=2, d=√184, it is 3. Both configurations have the required tangent mean12.
problems.answer: The harmonic mean is not uniquely determined.
problems.note: A centre distance or another independent condition is missing. The admissible radius range is 0<r<2√6, so the harmonic mean can vary over(0,3√6).

problems.title: Altitude of a13–14–15 triangle
problems.question: Find the altitude to the middle-length side of a triangle with sides 13,14,15.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: Heron’s formula with semiperimeter21 gives are a √(21·8·7·6)=84.
steps: The middle side is 14, so altitude=2·84/14=12.

problems.title: Simplify nested reciprocal radicals
problems.question: Simplify1/(√x+√y)² ÷ [((√x−√y)/(x−y))⁻¹−((x−y)/(x√x−y√y))⁻¹] ÷(1/√x−1/√y), then use x=0.025, y=0.1.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: Put u=√x, v=√y. The bracket becomes(u+v)−(u²+uv+v²)/(u+v)=uv/(u+v).
steps: After the first division, the expression is 1/[uv(u+v)]. Dividing by 1/u−1/v=(v−u)/(uv) gives 1/[(u+v)(v−u)]=1/(y−x).
At the supplied values, this is 1/0.075=40/3.
problems.note: The original expression requires x, y>0 and x≠y; the supplied values satisfy these conditions.

problems.title: Minimize a radical reciprocal
problems.question: Minimize√b/√a−(b−1)/√(ab) for positive a, b with 2a+18b=25.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: The expression simplifies to 1/√(ab). AM–GM gives(2a)(18b)≤(25/2)², so ab≤625/144.
steps: Therefore1/√(ab)≥12/25. Equality occurs at 2a=18b=25/2, or a=25/4, b=25/36.

problems.title: Construct a square-root length
problems.question: Given a segment of length a, construct a segment of length √15·a with compass and unmarked straightedge.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: The altitude to a diameter in a semicircle satisfies h²=pq, where p, q are the two diameter pieces.
steps: Step off 3 copies of a to obtain AD=3a, and 5 more to obtain DB=5a on one line. Construct the midpoint of AB and the circle with diameter AB.
At D, construct the perpendicular to AB and let it meet the semicircle at P. Then DP²=AD·DB=15a², so DP=√15·a.
problems.answer: The perpendicular segment DP has length √15·a.

problems.title: Chord joining tangent contacts
problems.question: A circle has radius 30 cm. Tangents from a point 50 cm from its centre touch at A, B. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: The tangent length is √(50²−30²)=40. The right-triangle altitude from either contact to the centre-external-point line is 30·40/50=24.
steps: The contact chord is perpendicular to that line and bisected by it, so AB=2·24=48 cm.

problems.title: Minimum isosceles-trapezoid perimeter
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has obtuse angle 150°, and height times midline9. Find its least perimeter.
problems.idea: Use exact radical identities, similarity, and bounds; check that the information determines the requested quantity.
formulas: Its acute angle is 30°. With height h, each leg is h/sin30°=2h, and midline m=9/h. Thus P=2m+4h=18/h+4h.
steps: This is feasible:the half-base difference h cot30° is less than m, so both bases are positive.
